For a short leg, self-adhesive felt pads stacked to the right thickness work well and stay hidden. For a loose wooden joint, remove the leg if possible, add wood glue into the joint, clamp it overnight, and reinsert. As a last resort, a small furniture leg leveler screwed into the bottom of the short leg gives adjustable height."}

Day 2 onward: Discard half the mixture, then feed with 50g flour (all-purpose is fine after day 2) and 50g water, stirring well, once daily. You'll likely see small bubbles by day 3-4 as wild yeast activates — this is normal and not yet 'ready.' By day 7-10, it should reliably double in size within 4-8 hours of feeding and smell pleasantly sour/yeasty rather than harsh. That doubling test is the real readiness signal, not just the number of days — trust the rise over the calendar."}

import subprocess, json

entries = [

Mix with a fork until crumbly, then knead with your palms for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic — this is the most important step. Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes at room temp. Cut dough into quarters, keep the rest covered. Roll one quarter thin (about 1/16 inch) — if it tears, rest it 10 more minutes and try again. Lightly dust with flour, fold loosely like a letter, and cut into strips with a knife or pizza wheel. Unfold, shake off excess flour, and cook in generously salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until it floats.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'How do I unclog a kitchen sink drain without calling a plumber?',
        'response': 'Start by removing any visible debris from the strainer. Boil a full kettle of water and carefully pour it straight down the drain — this often clears grease-based clogs. If that doesnt work, mix 1/2 cup baking soda with 1/2 cup white vinegar and pour the baking soda in first, then the vinegar. Cover the drain and let it fizz for 15 minutes, then flush with another kettle of boiling water. For a stubborn clog, use a hand-crank drain snake: insert it through the drain, crank clockwise while pushing down, until you feel the blockage, then pull it out. As a preventive measure, pour 1/4 cup of baking soda down the drain weekly followed by hot water to keep things clear.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'Give me a foolproof recipe for perfect scrambled eggs every time.',
        'response': 'Crack 2-3 eggs per person into a bowl, add a tiny pinch of salt and pepper, and whisk until fully blended (no streaks of white). Use a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat — high heat is the #1 mistake. Add 1 tbsp butter and let it foam, then pour in the eggs. Let them sit 10 seconds, then stir gently from the edges toward the center with a silicone spatula. Keep stirring slowly every 10-15 seconds, scraping the bottom, until large soft curds form and the eggs look slightly underdone — about 3-4 minutes total. Remove from heat immediately; the residual warmth will finish cooking them to perfect creaminess. A pat of butter stirred in at the end adds silkiness.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'How can I learn to change a flat tire by myself? Walk me through it step by step.',
        'response': 'Before you leave home, locate your spare tire, jack, and lug wrench in your vehicle. When you get a flat, pull over to a level, solid surface away from traffic and set the parking brake. Remove the hubcap if present by prying it off with the flat end of your lug wrench. Loosen (dont remove) each lug nut 1/4 turn counterclockwise while the tire is still on the ground. Position the jack at the manufacturers recommended lift point near the flat tire, and raise the car until the tire clears the ground. Now fully remove the lug nuts, pull off the flat tire, and mount the spare — hand-tighten the lug nuts in a star pattern. Lower the car until the tire just touches ground, then fully tighten the nuts in star pattern. Fully lower the car and give each nut one final tightening. Have a mechanic reinstall your real tire as soon as possible — most spares are not for long-distance driving.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'What is a good method for freezing meals ahead so I can just grab-and-go during a busy week?',
        'response': 'The key is choosing freezer-friendly dishes: soups, stews, chili, casseroles, and cooked grains all freeze well. Avoid creamy sauces and raw egg-based mixtures, which separate or become grainy when frozen. Cook your meal as usual, but slightly under-salt it since flavors mute when frozen. Let food cool completely at room temp (no more than 2 hours for safety), then portion into airtight containers or heavy freezer bags. Lay bags flat on a baking sheet to freeze — this creates space-saving bricks. Label everything with the date and contents; most cooked meals keep 3 months. To reheat, thaw overnight in the fridge, then warm on the stove or in the microwave, adding a splash of broth or water if it looks dry.'
    }
]

for entry in entries:
    subprocess.run(['python3', 'scripts/add_entry.py'], input=json.dumps(entry), text=True)

Lightly dust with flour, fold loosely like a letter, and cut into strips with a knife or pizza wheel. As a preventive measure, pour 1/4 cup of baking soda down the drain weekly followed by hot water to keep things clear.

Remove from heat immediately; the residual warmth will finish cooking them to perfect creaminess. A pat of butter stirred in at the end adds silkiness.

Lower the car until the tire just touches ground, then fully tighten the nuts in star pattern. Fully lower the car and give each nut one final tightening. Have a mechanic reinstall your real tire as soon as possible — most spares are not for long-distance driving.
